lessons: Never repeat the video title word-for-word as the opening hook line (e.g., repeating the title lost 34.0% in Garlic and 31.9% in Potatoes right at the start).
Cut generic filler sentences immediately following the hook (e.g., 'They are not just there to look cool' lost 31.5% in Windshield Dots; 'They look like similar fruits' lost 30.0% in Fruits Float).
Avoid interactive delays like 'Pause and guess' or countdowns (e.g., 'Pause and guess...' caused drops of 15.2% in Foil and 8.3% in Maple Syrup).

Lead with extreme claims or stark visual contrasts to maximize retention (e.g., 'older than the United States' achieved 1.85 10% retention; comparing tuna red meat to cod white meat achieved 0.86 vs similar at the end).

Delay complex jargon and technical explanations until after the hook is payoff-oriented (e.g., introducing sap percentage math early dropped 33.3% in Maple Syrup; abstract skin volume loss dropped 10.3% in Pruning Fingers).
worst_moment_types: Verbatim repetition of the title in the opening line
Generic filler transitions that add no new information
Explicit user interruptions (e.g., 'Pause and guess' prompts and countdowns)
Dense technical setup or dry background math presented too early
best_hook_types: Extreme historical or numerical scale comparisons (e.g., 'older than the United States')
Direct visual or categorical paradoxes (e.g., tuna vs. cod meat color)
Counter-intuitive everyday physical sensory facts (e.g., touching 400-degree hot foil)
